name: Looksminning

card.summary: Community term for deliberately downplaying, hiding or accepting a flaw in appearance, used to talk about trade-offs between looks and other goals.

quick.overview:
Looksminning (or looksmin) is looksmax.org slang for anything that lowers how good someone looks, in contrast to looksmaxxing, which raises it. Members use it for habits, features and procedures: a flat back of the head, a neck cyst, a coffee habit, drinking, screens, or exercise styles thought to look awkward.

It works as a way of weighing costs. Someone asks whether a thing is a looksmin before deciding whether to do it, treat it, or accept it. Because the term is informal, there is no research on it as such; threads are opinion and anecdote.
quick.how: In practice people post a candidate (a hairstyle limit, a supplement, a medical condition, a workout) and others say how big a looksmin they think it is. Some threads advise avoiding the habit, others describe fixing the feature, for example by haircuts that disguise a flat occiput or surgery for a neck cyst.
quick.risks: The term itself carries no risk, but advice in these threads is informal and sometimes involves medical conditions or procedures. Several threads concern conditions (a thyroglossal duct cyst, gynecomastia) for which clinicians are the usual source of diagnosis and treatment.

lead: Looksminning, usually shortened to looksmin, is a term used on the looksmax.org forum for anything that is seen as reducing a person's attractiveness, the opposite of looksmaxxing. It is applied both to personal features and to choices or habits, and can also describe weighing a possible downside before a decision [1][2][3].

Threads using the word cover a wide range: a thyroglossal duct cyst in the neck that a poster says affected his side profile [1], a flat back of the head and the haircuts that suit it [2], whether jumping rope in a gym looks awkward [3], and whether coffee, drinking, screens, minoxidil, wisdom tooth extraction or palate expanders count [4][5][6][7][8]. The common thread is a cost-benefit question about looks.
The term is community slang and has no formal definition or research literature.

chain: Name a flaw or habit that may lower looks
Judge whether it is worth fixing, hiding or accepting
Choose haircuts, treatment or behavior accordingly
angle.text: The concept gives members a vocabulary for spotting things that may detract from appearance and for deciding what to do about them, for example choosing a haircut that offsets a flat occiput or seeking removal of a visible neck cyst.

paras: A looksmin is a feature, habit or choice thought to reduce looks. Posters rate it informally, with phrases such as a "hard looksmin" for a large downside [4]. Threads ask whether everyday things such as raw milk or screen time belong in the category [5][6].

Some threads ask the question the other way, whether a benefit is worth the looksmin: one asks if drinking is worth it [7] and another debates whether minoxidil is a looksmin or an overhyped aid [8][9].

A poster described a thyroglossal duct cyst, a congenital remnant of the thyroid's embryonic path, saying it affected his neck profile and that he planned to have it removed [1]. Another poster described a flat occiput and said short haircuts fit poorly, recommending a blowout taper or mullet to add back volume [2].

A thread on jump rope asks whether the exercise looks awkward to onlookers while noting its calorie burn [3]. Other threads ask about gynecomastia, wisdom tooth removal and palate expanders [10][11][12].
No studies found. The term is forum slang and has not been studied.

lore.intro: Members use looksmin as a quick label for a possible appearance downside, usually in titled threads asking whether something qualifies [3][4].

claims.claim: Features like a flat occiput are "looksmins" that limit hairstyles
claims.believers: Posters say a flat back of the head rules out most short cuts and is best offset by volume at the back [2].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined hairstyle suitability for occipital shape.

claims.claim: A visible neck cyst can lower facial aesthetics
claims.believers: One poster said a thyroglossal duct cyst bulged when he spoke and affected his side profile [1].
claims.experts: Thyroglossal duct cysts are a recognized congenital condition managed by clinicians; no study addresses their effect on perceived attractiveness.
